figures.caption: Figure 1: Multi-view relational distillation (MVRD). (a) Spatial reasoning. MVRD with Dual Pathway variant approaches the feature fusion method VLM-3R [1], using the same backbone and dataset, with far fewer added parameters and lower latency. (b) Scene understanding. MVRD transfers to scene understanding, surpassing the prior state-of-the-art 3DRS [2] in all tasks.

Figure 2: Failure of feature distillation. (a) Qualitative: At layer 20, 3DRS* fails to align microwave with the corresponding visual patches, unlike the base model LLaVA-Video-7B-Qwen2. (b) Quantitative: A sharp drop in text-based object-detection precision across layers indicates severe degradation in vision-language alignment.
Figure 3: An overview of multi-view relational distillation loss and dual pathway.
Table 3: Ablation on distillation target and dual pathway. Feat Dist means feature distillation.

Figure 4: Vision-language alignment across methods. (a) At distillation layer, MVRD and MVRD + Dual Pathway align microwave with its visual patches better than feature distillation. (b) Both improve vision-language alignment while matching feature distillation in geometric relation modeling.
Figure 5: Row-wise Correlation of cosine distance from VGGT with 3D Euclidean distance on ScanNet validation set.
Table 8: Training hyperparameters for the spatial-reasoning experiments on the VLM-3R [1] dataset.
Table 10: Training configuration for the 3D scene-understanding experiments.
Table 11: Comparison of 3DRS [2] and the SFT baselines [26, 1] on VSI-Bench

Table 12: Per-task VSI-Bench results across VLM backbones. “Feature. Dist.” denotes feature distillation; “MVRD” is our relational distillation. “+ DP” marks Dual Pathway. Best per column within each backbone block is in bold.
